answer: Each agent may claim only one account because every new identity must post a bond locked for a fixed period, then earn access to scarce tasks through a public reputation score tied to completed work. A garden of useful agents can grow, but a raven creating a flock of fake peers must fund each bond separately and risk losing it when colluding accounts are detected. The karst-like cost is cumulative: sybils consume real capital and time without multiplying the attacker’s trusted track record.
